title: Saving a recording somewhere else goes through the same sheet everything else does
goal: Every picture and every icon in Photonz leaves through one Export sheet: you pick the format there, you see the choices that format has, and the sheet tells you what the file is going to weigh before you commit to it. A recording is the one thing in the app that does none of that. Save As on a recording throws a bare system save box at you with the format already decided, no choices, and no idea how big the thing you are about to send is going to be. A screen recording is the file most likely to be too big to send, so it is the worst one to say nothing about.
notes:
FOUND BY READING, manager pass 2026-09-19, HEAD e9d6b163. Not a crash, so no reproduction run: the two code paths are simply different and can be read side by side.

The picture path: Sources/Photonz/ExportDialog.swift. It carries the format rows, the quality control, and a weigher that encodes the picture off the main actor to say what it will really weigh (byteCount, weighing, weighed, saysWhatTheVectorWeighs around lines 91 to 340). Two tasks landed that behaviour deliberately and recently: da51700a "A PNG says what it will weigh before you save it" and a4a7dbf7 "An SVG says what it will weigh too". So the pattern is established, shipped and not speculative.

The recording path: AppCoordinator.saveRecording at AppCoordinator.swift:389. It builds an NSSavePanel by hand, sets allowedContentTypes from a format that was already chosen by which menu item you picked, runs it modally, and exports. No sheet, no weight, no choices. The format is decided in EditorCommands.swift around 334 to 348, where MP4, GIF and HEIC are three separate menu items and only GIF and HEIC carry a quality submenu. MP4 has no quality control at all: VideoExporter.exportMP4 is pinned to AVAssetExportPresetHighestQuality (VideoExporter.swift around :208).

Why this is not competitor parity dressing. The user described the whole job on 2026-09-18 as "I just want to trim, save, send in teams", and the thing that stops a screen recording being sent is its size. The app already decided that saying what a file will weigh is worth doing; this is carrying that decision to the one format where it bites hardest, not inventing a new idea.

DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE, and say so in the audit: choosing a SMALLER mp4, by resolution or bitrate, is a new control the user has not asked for and it needs a decision card before anybody builds it. This task is about one way out of the app, not about new knobs. If the runner comes to believe the size choice is the whole point, stop and open a card rather than build it.

WHY IT DEPENDS ON THE p0: trim-a-recording-save-it-send-it-the-whole-flow works on saveRecording as the current way out ("while this is broken the way out is Save As"). Landing a rewrite of that path underneath it would collide. Let the p0 finish first.
acceptance: Saving a copy of a recording opens the same Export sheet as a picture does, with the recording formats in it rather than a bare save box
The formats a recording already supports are all reachable from that one sheet instead of from three different menu items: video, animated GIF and HEIC
The quality choice that GIF and HEIC already have lives in the sheet beside the format, where the picture quality control lives, rather than in a submenu you pick before the save box appears

The sheet says what the file will weigh wherever it can honestly say it, using the weighing the sheet already does; where it genuinely cannot know without encoding the whole recording, it says what it does know and does not invent a number
Cancelling the sheet writes nothing and leaves the recording and its edits exactly as they were
A saved copy carries the trim and the crop, checked by reading the duration and the dimensions of the file that lands rather than trusting the app
Exporting an untrimmed recording still takes the fast path and does not re-encode
The picture export sheet is unchanged: every existing export walk still passes
Ships behind a named flag so it can be turned off, and the try steps are in the task log: open a recording from History, choose Save As, and the sheet appears
A walk covers opening the sheet from a recording and saving a copy

Audit under queue/audits/ with the sheet photographed for each format, and anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar and written into this task log if it does not

log.note: Noticed while fixing the trim/save flow on 2026-09-19: ⇧⌘S on a recording is the only route to a copy, and it goes straight to a bare NSSavePanel with the format already decided. Worth knowing for this task: the action behind that menu item and its dimming used to disagree about which editor they were talking about (the action preferred the image editor unconditionally), which is now fixed in EditorCommands, so whatever replaces the panel can trust that Save As is talking about the recording in front of you.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, before building. (1) Walking it as a first-timer: record, trim, hit ⇧⌘S to send it to somebody. Today that is a bare save box with MP4 already decided. The picture flow is Export sheet then save box, two dialogs, and nobody complains about that, so putting a sheet in front of the recording's save box costs a keystroke and buys the format choice and the size. Consistent, so build it. (2) What the picture sheet assumes that video cannot deliver: the weigher. ExportSizer really encodes the picture, a few hundred ms. There is no honest equivalent for a GIF or a HEIC, because weighing one IS encoding the whole recording, minutes for a long clip. So the sheet must degrade honestly rather than show a formula. Decision taken: MP4 unedited is EXACT (it is a verbatim file copy, so it is the source file's own byte count); MP4 edited is ABOUT, from the source file's own bytes-per-second times the kept seconds times the pixel-area ratio when cropped, both measured ratios rather than invented constants, and the word 'about' is on the line; GIF and HEIC say what they do know (output pixels, frame rate, kept length) and say plainly that the size is not known until it is written. That is acceptance item 4 read literally. (3) Cut as decorative: no scale row (1x/2x means nothing for a recording), no Include the background row, no Where it is going row. Three rows only: Format, Quality for the two formats that have one, and the size line where the picture sheet's size line sits. (4) Shortest version with the same value: the sheet only CHOOSES. Export… still hands off to the existing NSSavePanel and the existing exporter, so no export engine is touched and the fast path stays the fast path. (5) Collision found: File ▸ Export… (⇧⌘E) is dimmed whenever there is no image document, so today a recording window has no Export command at all and the three Export items live in the Video menu instead. With the flag on, ⇧⌘E opens the recording sheet in a video window, the Video menu's three Export items collapse to one Export…, and Save As on a recording opens the same sheet. That is acceptance items 1 and 2. (6) MP4 quality stays out, exactly as the task says: no new knobs, and the sheet shows no Quality row for MP4 the same way it shows no slider for PNG.

BUILT AND VERIFIED. Core: Sources/PhotonzCore/RecordingExport.swift decides what the sheet may say (21 tests, Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/RecordingExportTests.swift, written before the code). Sheet: Sources/Photonz/RecordingExportDialog.swift; its rows and metrics come from the new Sources/Photonz/ExportSheetRow.swift, which ExportDialog now uses too, so the picture sheet renders identically and the two cannot drift. Wiring in EditorCommands: Save As on a recording, File ▸ Export… (⇧⌘E now alive in a video window) and a single Video ▸ Export… replacing the three Export items, all flag gated on next-recording-export-sheet. AppCoordinator.saveRecording split into the save box plus writeRecording(_:as:quality:to:), which is the part a walk can call. ACCEPTANCE, item by item. 1 and 2: the sheet opens with MP4, GIF and HEIC in one segmented row, photographed for each. 3: the size preset is a Quality row beside the format, gone entirely for MP4 exactly as the slider is gone for PNG. 4: an untouched MP4 is a verbatim copy so its size is EXACT (the sheet read 'MP4 Video · 130 KB' and the file that landed was 130 KB); a trimmed or cropped one says 'about', from the recording's own bytes per second times the pixel share, both measured (the sheet said 'about 16 KB' and 16531 bytes landed); GIF and HEIC say 'size not known until it is written' rather than a guess, while everything else about them is live — pressing Small moved the line from 800 × 500 · 15 fps to 480 × 300 · 10 fps. 5: Cancel after trying three formats and a preset left the recording at 8s, the file on disk at 8s and no preserved original, because nothing was committed. 6: writeRecording opens the file that landed — 'recording-export-trimmed.mp4 is 16 KB, it runs 4.0s at 640 × 400 px, re-encoded', against a 1280 × 800 8s recording, so trim and crop both reached the disk rather than being taken on the app's word. 7: 'recording-export-whole.mp4 runs 8.0s at 1280 × 800 px, byte for byte the recording itself, so nothing was re-encoded'. 8: png-export-size, png-export-background, export-quality, export-webp, svg-export and the four other svg export walks all still pass. 10: Scripts/playtest/recording-export-sheet-walk.json, 55 steps, ok in 12s, five real screen captures. 11: queue/audits/2026-09-19-recording-export-sheet.json with four captures beside it. Scripts/test.sh green.

REVIEW OF THE BUILT THING, and what is left rough. Ran it as a person would, on the probe, with the sheet photographed at every format. What is good: the sheet is three short rows and two lines, it reads as the picture sheet, and the preset finally SHOWS what it does — in the submenu you picked High or Small blind, and here the line under it answers 800 × 500 · 15 fps or 480 × 300 · 10 fps before you commit. What is left rough, each with where it went. (a) There is still no way to make an MP4 smaller: the sheet can say 200 MB and offer nothing to do about it. The task put that deliberately out of scope and said it needs a decision card rather than a runner's guess, and I agree — the sheet delivers real value without it, so I did not open a card on my own initiative. It is the first item of the audit's rough list, where the user's reaction becomes the task. NOT filed. (b) The sheet is headed Export even when you reached it through Save As. Deliberate: for a recording, saving a copy somewhere else IS the export and there is only one sheet. A wording choice worth disagreeing with, so it is in the audit rather than in a task. (c) The estimate is measured off the recording itself, which on the synthetic eight second sample was within three percent; a busy screen recording may drift further, which is what the word 'about' is carrying. In the audit for the user to judge. (d) LEFT ROUGH, no task: the keyboard and menu routes in (⇧⌘S, File ▸ Export…, Video ▸ Export…) were wired and read but never PRESSED, because the Mac's screen was locked for this whole run and macOS freezes a background app's menu bar under a lock — save-is-live-after-a-trim-walk failed on exactly that in the same session, and the standing p1 confirm-file-save-is-live-on-a-trimmed-recording already covers 'somebody has to press this on an unlocked screen'. Everything on the sheet itself, and every file it writes, was driven and read back for real. It is try step 2 of the audit and the last line of its rough list. (e) LEFT ROUGH, no task: three export walks and one trim walk failed in this session and all four fail on step kinds a lock is known to stop — panelMenu in icon-export-animated-walk, a tutorial waitFor in tutorial-export-a-spec-list-walk and tutorial-save-export-copy-walk, and a window-scoped ⌘S in save-is-live-after-a-trim-walk. Artifacts of forcing the walks, not findings, and none of them touches this code path.

One behaviour change worth knowing, outside the sheet. The fast path used to copy the file with try? and no reporting, so a copy that failed (no room, no permission on the folder) did nothing at all and said nothing. It now runs through the same Task as the re-encode, so a failure reaches reportExportFailure and the person is told. The cost is that isExportingRecording flickers true for the length of a file copy, which is what the progress affordance is for anyway.
